body:
Scope: independent direction review of the complete compact-retirement proposal and its embedded feasibility, including the incoming shortlist and preparatory audit. Selected recording contract is rigorloop-records-v2 in this new root; it does not migrate or supersede an old root. Actual runtime and standing authority were inspected because feasibility depends on existing support, rather than module names or installed skill assumptions.

Core dimensions: challenge pass (multiple supported semantic engines carry maintenance and compatibility obligations); goals pass (bounded supported-surface reduction with honest protection and distinct measurements); scope pass (one compact creation/mutation/progression engine plus required reading/recovery/creation/projection dependencies); principle pass (explicit compatibility disposition before removal); direction pass (concrete enough to investigate without approving handler deletion); feasibility pass for Design only (separate dispatch exists but active creation, projection eligibility and transaction recovery are coupled); impact pass (stranded work, surviving recovery and limited deletion benefit disclosed); downstream authority pass (commands, diagnostics, continuation, rollout and proof allocation remain Design/Delivery); requested decision pass (Design direction only, no cutover, current recorder retirement or implementation permission).

Vision alignment: aligned. Traceable historical interpretation, independent review, preserved recovery and explicit compatibility decisions support durable, inspectable and resumable work. Retiring a semantic engine is compatible with that vision only when the promised continuation and recovery boundary is established before disabling its sole supported path. The proposal states that condition instead of silently equating recorder availability with a replacement workflow engine.

Scope preservation and specialized gate: scope_budget_context applies to the incoming multi-workstream shortlist. The table separates preparatory duplicate/rollout audit, the compact core and its dependencies, other historical engines, automation/calibration, release tooling, further test consolidation and excluded recorder safety/v1 compatibility. Deferred work has named owners and separate destinations; no unmentioned follow-on deletion is authorized. No missing-standing-artifact or vision-exception gate applies. The previous thirteen-suite deletion remains disclosed coverage loss, not evidence that runtime was retired. The current proposal does not restore or expand those removals automatically.

Independent feasibility observations: canonical activation explicitly says active and packaged bytes agree. new-change consumes compactWriterStatus; CLI dispatch separates recording, compact and historical lifecycle. Compact operations import eligibility, projection imports progression/permitted-operation eligibility, and compact CLI imports both projection/evaluation and transaction inspection/recovery. Current CLI Design expressly preserves those handlers and excludes them as deletion targets for the prior initiative. Thus this is a new compatibility direction, not a continuation of previously approved deletion. The governing retirement contract requires protected-failure/fixture disposition, old/replacement comparison, explicit de-contracting and rollback; its fixed vocabulary and adoption scope must be reconciled in Design rather than silently extended or replaced by another ledger.

Known limitations: independently reran workflow-context --format json and observed exit2 blocked RL_CONTEXT_CHANGE_INVALID for 2026-04-24-multi-agent-adapters-first-public-release with an empty candidates array. That array proves no absence of active work. Authoritative continuation inventory and external support assumptions remain unresolved pre-cutover conditions. The ten retained activation/public-CLI tests are bounded existing-boundary proof, not exhaustive caller or retirement proof. The rollout audit exposes a pre-existing failing M4 source-string assertion while the other four cases pass; all five remain unchanged. This failure is explicit negative evidence against withheld-activation assumptions, not an introduced duplicate-correction regression or an overall green branch result.

The audit distinctions are justified by actual assertions: mixed historical prose and live forbidden/existence checks need separation; historical scaffolding prose can be considered only under its own disposition; current section/result/handoff assertions protect enduring live behavior; unsupported --json rejection remains a current interface boundary. Milestone naming alone supports none of their removal. No material proposal defect or necessary direction-level owner decision remains. These implementation/cutover conditions do not prevent a responsible decision to pursue bounded detailed Design.

No proposal edit recommended as a required correction. Return at the isolated proposal-review boundary. This judgment settles only direction sufficiency, not detailed Design, retirement adoption, implementation, final Verify, branch/PR readiness or automatic downstream continuation. The separate preparatory correction has its own scoped code assessment.
independence_basis: Separate delegated reviewer /root/independent_proposal_review did not author this proposal or preparatory correction. Independently inspected exact subjects, actual existing implementation boundaries and evidence; writes only review judgments, not authoring or routing state.
